sections.h2: Where is Toombs County and what towns does it include?
sections.html:
Toombs County lies in southeast Georgia, with Lyons as the county seat and Vidalia as the largest city. The legislature formed it on August 18, 1905, as the 144th county, and it was organized that October, according to Wikipedia.

Its land came from Tattnall and Montgomery counties, and a small piece of Emanuel County was added in 1907 to give it today's lines. The county is 371 square miles, mostly land. Its southern half, running south of Vidalia, drains into the Altamaha River sub-basin, while the northern half around Lyons drains into the Ohoopee River sub-basin.

Incorporated places are Lyons, Santa Claus and Vidalia, with Ohoopee as a census-designated place. Smaller communities include Center, English Eddy, Normantown and South Thompson. The county shares borders with Emanuel, Candler, Tattnall, Appling, Jeff Davis, Montgomery and Treutlen counties. Vidalia is part of the same micropolitan area as the county, and the Toombs County School District operates the public schools.

sections.h2: How affordable are homes in Toombs County?
sections.html:
Toombs County has the lowest home values of the four counties in this group. QuickFacts lists a median owner-occupied value of $137,000 for 2020-2024, and 60.5% of housing units are owner-occupied.

Only 35 building permits were issued in 2025, so the supply of new homes is thin, and most sales are of existing houses. The 2020 census counted 10,505 households and 12,027 housing units, with 12.7% vacant and a 9.5% rental vacancy rate. Estimates put the population at 27,545 in mid-2025, up 1.9% from the 2020 base. QuickFacts puts the poverty rate at 22.8%, the highest of the four counties, and 16.3% of residents under 65 have no health insurance.

sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Toombs County?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner collects and the tax assessors value. The tax commissioner's office is at 100 Courthouse Square, Suite 169, in Lyons, GA 30436, and the phone is (912) 526-8575. Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

The county tax site's FAQ gives (912) 526-6291 for the board of tax assessors, which handles values, returns and exemptions. A copy of your warranty deed comes from the deed room of the Clerk of Superior Court in the courthouse.

  • Tax commissioner: bills, payments, mobile home decals, tax sales
  • Board of tax assessors: values, returns, homestead, appeals
  • Board of Equalization: hears appeals of assessor values, appointed by the Grand Jury
  • Board of Commissioners and Board of Education: set the county and school millage rates

The county site says the commissioner does not set values or rates. A complaint about the size of the bill belongs with the elected boards that levy it.

sections.h2: When is Toombs County property tax due and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Two county pages give different dates. The general information page says bills are mailed by October 20 and are payable by December 20, while the FAQ says real estate and business personal property tax has been due November 15 since 2018.

Read the due date printed on your own bill, and call (912) 526-8575 if in doubt. The FAQ lists interest of 1% per month after the due date and a 10% penalty on tax unpaid 90 days past it. Once taxes sit unpaid for more than 30 days, a fi. fa. lien can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, which the FAQ notes is public and can affect credit.

  • Real estate: interest of 1% monthly after the due date
  • Penalty: 10% when not paid within 90 days
  • Lien: may be recorded after 30 days unpaid
  • Mobile homes: due April 1, with a 10% filing penalty and 1% per month

The commissioner's tax sales page announced a December 2, 2025 sale on the courthouse steps at 10 a.m., which is now past. The listing for any sale is available at the office, so ask for the current schedule.

sections.h2: What should a Toombs County seller do about the tax bill?
sections.html:
Ask the commissioner's office for a written balance for the parcel before you sign a contract. Georgia gives no partial-year refund, so whoever owned the home on January 1 owes the whole year, the state revenue department says.

Lyons and Vidalia are cities, and a house inside one may carry city tax in addition to county tax, so ask whether both apply. A seller who is behind should also check the Clerk of Superior Court for a recorded lien, since a title company will want it cleared. If the roof, plumbing or wiring needs work that you cannot afford, selling as-is to a cash buyer avoids the repair bill, and the unpaid tax gets settled at closing from the price.

A clear payoff letter and a copy of the deed from the courthouse are the two papers that speed a closing along most.

sections.h2: Which Toombs County homestead exemptions are listed?
sections.html:
The county's general information page prints the amounts for its regular homestead exemption. For an owner who lives in the home before January 1, it lists $20,000 off the assessed value for county operations, $2,000 off county school tax, and $2,000 off the state portion. A home inside a city gets $10,000 off the city and city school tax.

Several age and veteran categories exist, and the page labels them S3 for 62 and older with an income test, S4 and SC for 65 and older, S5 for disabled veterans, SS for unremarried surviving spouses, and a local exemption for age 70 and over on school tax. The 62-and-over school exemption has a $10,000 earned-income test for the prior year. Details differ by category, so ask the assessors which one fits.

Applications run from January 1 through April 1, and Georgia law gives no extension. Once approved, an exemption renews each year until eligibility changes. If you move, you must file again for the new address.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Toombs County assessment?
sections.html:
Appeal in writing to the Toombs County Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the date on the notice. Notices usually go out in the spring, per the county site.

The appeal can cover taxability, value, uniformity, or the denial of an exemption. You choose the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator, and the case can go on to Superior Court after that. For mobile homes, the county says a different value can be declared within 45 days of the bill mailing, and a further appeal to the Board of Equalization is allowed within 21 days of the change notice.

faqs.q: What number reaches the Toombs County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: Call (912) 526-8575. The office is at 100 Courthouse Square, Suite 169, Lyons, and it is open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Is Toombs County tax due in November or December?
faqs.a: The county's own pages disagree: one says December 20 and the FAQ says November 15. Follow the date printed on your bill and call the commissioner's office to confirm it.

faqs.q: What happens if a Toombs County bill is paid late?
faqs.a: Interest of 1% per month is added after the due date, and a 10% penalty applies to tax unpaid 90 days past it. After 30 days, a lien can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court.

faqs.q: When do Toombs County mobile home taxes come due?
faqs.a: April 1 each year. After that date a 10% filing penalty and 1% monthly charge apply, and the owner must pay in full to obtain a location permit and decal.

faqs.q: How long do I have to dispute a Toombs County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice. File in writing with the Board of Tax Assessors and say whether you want the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator.
